_note: Checked against primary sources on 2026-11-15. Quotes and section numbers for each entry are in docs/sources.md. The law watcher (rules/feeds.json) flags entries that official news may have changed; a person re-reads the source and updates the entry and its last_checked date.

rules.instrument: MHA procedure of 2 January 2026, section 9.1 (police directions under BNSS sections 168 and 94)
rules.summary: When a fraud report reaches the bank, it holds the reported amount, or the part of it still in the account, not the whole balance. Suspending digital banking or seizing the account is for accounts reported multiple times, and needs separate lawful directions from the police.
rules.source_name: MHA SOP for NCRP-CFCFRMS, Custody, Restoration of Money and Grievance Redressal (2 January 2026), as annexed to the Meghalaya High Court notification of 28 April 2026

rules.summary: For a held amount, the account holder complains at their bank, which must file the grievance within 7 calendar days. The police officer on the case must release the hold or record reasons within 15 calendar days; if they do not act, the grievance goes automatically to the District Grievance Officer, who decides within 15 calendar days.
rules.source_name: MHA SOP for NCRP-CFCFRMS, Custody, Restoration of Money and Grievance Redressal (2 January 2026), as annexed to the Meghalaya High Court notification of 28 April 2026

rules.summary: If no lawful direction to continue a contested hold arrives within 90 calendar days of the bank filing the grievance, the bank removes the hold on the account holder's request, unless the police ask to extend it by up to 90 more days.
rules.source_name: MHA SOP for NCRP-CFCFRMS, Custody, Restoration of Money and Grievance Redressal (2 January 2026), as annexed to the Meghalaya High Court notification of 28 April 2026

rules.summary: The bank checks the account holder's explanation and files the grievance on the government's online Grievance Redressal Module, where the police record their decision. The module has been running since April 2026.
rules.source_name: MHA SOP of 2 January 2026, section 10.1; PIB release 2287674 (22 July 2026)

rules.summary: When the account holder asks, the bank may tell them which police unit ordered the hold and how to contact it. This is not treated as tipping off. The complainant's details are never shared.
rules.source_name: MHA SOP for NCRP-CFCFRMS, Custody, Restoration of Money and Grievance Redressal (2 January 2026), as annexed to the Meghalaya High Court notification of 28 April 2026

rules.instrument: MHA procedure of 2 January 2026, sections 9.5 and 10.1(a)
rules.summary: The account holder gives the bank their explanation of the payment, and the bank weighs it before filing the grievance. Where a payment aggregator or e-commerce company is involved, it is expected to upload the settlement and order details. The procedure lists no fixed set of documents.
rules.source_name: MHA SOP for NCRP-CFCFRMS, Custody, Restoration of Money and Grievance Redressal (2 January 2026), as annexed to the Meghalaya High Court notification of 28 April 2026

rules.instrument: Supreme Court order of 4 August 2026, In Re: Victims of Digital Arrest, SMW(Crl) No. 3/2025
rules.summary: All States, Union Territories and police were directed to adopt and run the grievance and money-restoration modules of the 2 January 2026 procedure. A person should ordinarily try that grievance route first, but it does not bar any other legal remedy.
rules.source_name: Supreme Court of India, record of proceedings dated 4 August 2026

rules.summary: Police power to seize property suspected to be linked to an offence. High Courts are split on whether it lets police freeze a bank account without a Magistrate's order (Delhi, Bombay and Kerala say no; Allahabad and Karnataka say yes, Allahabad only up to the suspect amount). The Supreme Court has not decided the point.
rules.source_name: BNSS 2023, Gazette of India No. 54 of 25 December 2023; Delhi High Court, Malabar Gold and Diamond Ltd v. Union of India, 16 January 2026

rules.summary: To attach suspected proceeds of crime, police must apply to a Court or Magistrate, which normally gives 14 days' notice to show cause and a hearing, but may order an interim attachment without notice.
rules.source_name: BNSS 2023, Gazette of India No. 54 of 25 December 2023

rules.instrument: RBI draft (Know Your Customer) Amendment Directions, 2026, released 11 September 2026
rules.summary: Draft only, not in force. Banks could themselves hold a flagged transaction of ₹1,000 or more, give the customer 20 days to explain, decide within 30 days, and lift the hold on day 31 unless police instruct otherwise, with 60 days as the outer limit. It would not apply to nodal, pool or escrow accounts. The draft proposes a start of 1 April 2027; a Supreme Court order of 29 October 2026 expects final rules by the end of 2026.
rules.source_name: Reserve Bank of India press release 2026-2027/1109 and draft text

ladder.note: From the MHA procedure of 2 January 2026, section 10.1. Day counts assume the bank files on the last day it is allowed.

steps.to: Your bank branch, which files the grievance on the Grievance Redressal Module
steps.deadline: Files within 7 calendar days of your complaint

steps.to: The police officer on the case
steps.deadline: Releases the hold or records reasons within 15 calendar days

steps.to: The District Grievance Officer (Additional SP or Deputy SP rank)
steps.deadline: Gets the grievance automatically if the police officer does not act; decides within 15 calendar days
